name: Electrically Power-Assisted Cycle (Pedalec)
description: The 250 W branch of Australia's national e-bike definition, the EN 15194 pedelec, which the states' road rules make a bicycle: a pedal cycle whose electric motor of no more than 250 W continuous rated power assists less as it speeds up past 6 km/h and cuts out at 25 km/h, or above 6 km/h once the rider stops pedalling. Since December 2025 only one meeting EN 15194:2017 or later is excluded from the road vehicles regulated on import.

restrictions.rule: An electrically powered pedal cycle with a maximum continuous rated power of no more than 250 W
restrictions.citation: Vehicle Standard (Australian Design Rule – Definitions and Vehicle Categories) 2005, cl. 3 (definitions of electrically power-assisted cycle and power-assisted pedal cycle)

restrictions.rule: The motor's output is progressively reduced as it speeds up past 6 km/h, and cut off once it reaches 25 km/h
restrictions.citation: Vehicle Standard (Australian Design Rule – Definitions and Vehicle Categories) 2005, cl. 3 (definition of electrically power-assisted cycle)

restrictions.rule: The motor may propel it without pedalling, as a throttle or walk mode, only up to 6 km/h; past that it cuts off whenever the rider stops pedalling
restrictions.citation: Vehicle Standard (Australian Design Rule – Definitions and Vehicle Categories) 2005, cl. 3 (definition of electrically power-assisted cycle)
Vehicle Standard (Australian Design Rule – Definitions and Vehicle Categories) 2005, cl. 3 (definition of power-assisted pedal cycle)

restrictions.rule: Excluded from the two- and three-wheeled moped categories (LA and LB)
restrictions.citation: Vehicle Standard (Australian Design Rule – Definitions and Vehicle Categories) 2005, cls. 4.2.1, 4.2.2

restrictions.rule: Past these limits a two-wheeler is a motor vehicle: an electric one that can't exceed 50 km/h is an LA moped, a faster one an LC motorcycle, and it can be ridden on a road or path only once it meets the Australian Design Rules and is registered, with a licensed rider; a power or speed limit set by software or a switch doesn't bring it back within them
restrictions.citation: Vehicle Standard (Australian Design Rule – Definitions and Vehicle Categories) 2005, cls. 4.2.1, 4.2.3

restrictions.rule: The Australian Road Rules, the model the states' road rules follow, make it a bicycle, and exclude from bicycles any other vehicle with an auxiliary motor that can put out more than 200 W
restrictions.citation: Australian Road Rules, Dictionary (definition of bicycle); Road Safety Road Rules 2017 (Vic), Dictionary (definition of bicycle)

restrictions.rule: Ridden under the bicycle road rules, with no licence, registration or compulsory third-party insurance
Excluded from regulation as a road vehicle only if it meets EN 15194:2017 or a later edition; one meeting just the performance limits above may need a road vehicle approval to be imported
restrictions.citation: Road Vehicle Standards (Classes of Vehicles that are not Road Vehicles) Determination 2021, ss. 5(1), 6(h), as amended by F2025L01649; Road Vehicle Standards Act 2018, s. 6

restrictions.rule: Western Australia's 250 W pedalec is one meeting EN 15194:2009 or EN 15194:2009+A1:2011
restrictions.citation: Road Traffic (Administration) Act 2008 (WA), s. 4; Road Traffic (Administration) Regulations 2014 (WA), r. 4

restrictions.rule: In Western Australia, a rider under 16 must not ride one with the power assistance engaged
